item.title: People who opposed Tinubu now work with him — Fashola
item.description: Former Lagos State Governor Babatunde Fashola has said President Bola Tinubu’s ability to retain former allies and reconcile political opponents demonstrates his capacity to manage Nigeria’s diversity and build consensus. Fashola said politicians who opposed Tinubu in the past had now joined forces with him, describing the president’s ability to bring former adversaries together as evidence of his leadership and capacity to work with others. He spoke in an interview with ARISE News while responding to why Nigerians should give Tinubu another four years in office. The former minister of works said voters should assess the presidential candidates based on their relationships with people they previously worked with, arguing that the ability to sustain working relationships through difficult periods was an important measure of leadership. “The three main presidential candidates today share one trait in common. They all started as governors. One of them didn’t take office, but he was already a governor-elect, Vice President Atiku Abubakar. Where are all the people who worked with them today? That’s a job reference question for those who want to vote,” Fashola said. He asked why many of those who worked with Tinubu during his time as Lagos governor had remained with him, while political associates of other candidates had moved on. “Where are all the people who worked with these people? Why is it only President Tinubu that has all those who worked with him still with him? And they were with him for 16 years or so out of office when he wasn’t a president. That’s a very good answer to the question,” he said. Fashola said the loyalty of Tinubu’s associates reflected his ability to work with others and manage disagreements without abandoning relationships, adding that such qualities were important for a president leading a country with diverse interests. “It shows an ability to work with others. If you are going to get entrusted with managing Nigeria’s diverse family, you must be able to work in a team, and you don’t just get up and jump away when there is crisis in the fold,” he said. He contrasted Tinubu’s political experience with that of other candidates, saying the president remained in the APC despite internal crises, while others left the parties through which they rose to prominence. “There was crisis in the APC. He didn’t leave the party. The others have left the parties that brought them to prominence,” Fashola said. The former governor further argued that Tinubu had expanded his political alliances by bringing former opponents into his fold, including those who once strongly opposed him. “All the people who opposed Tinubu when he used to be called the last man standing. All of them are now working with him. Not just those who worked with him before; those who oppose him are now working with him,” he said. item.title: From fuel subsidy return to Ajaokuta revival, Atiku’s 2027 promises so far
item.description: Former Vice-President Atiku Abubakar has promised to restore petrol and electricity subsidies, tackle insecurity, create jobs and revive key infrastructure projects if elected president in 2027. The African Democratic Congress (ADC) presidential candidate has made the pledges at campaign rallies in Sokoto, Bauchi, Yobe and Kogi states, while presenting his proposed policies as measures to reduce the cost of living and improve economic conditions. At the ADC presidential campaign flag-off in Sokoto on November 4 , Atiku promised to restore petrol subsidy, reopen Nigeria’s land borders to encourage trade and tackle insecurity, including kidnapping, banditry and terrorism. He also pledged to reduce the cost of pilgrimage for Muslim and Christian faithful. Atiku said restoring petrol subsidy would help reduce transportation costs and ease the burden of rising prices of essential goods. He also argued that reopening the land borders would benefit farmers, traders and transport operators by stimulating cross-border commerce. At a rally in Bauchi State on November 14, Atiku extended his subsidy promise to electricity, saying he would restore both petroleum and electricity subsidies if elected. He also pledged to strengthen security, particularly in the North-East, resume oil exploration in the Kolmani field and continue the Mambilla Hydroelectric Power Project. “I will restore electricity subsidies. I also promise to restore security in the North-East sub-region and the country at large. I further promise to continue oil exploration activities in Kolmani so that we can have additional sources of revenue,” he said at the Bauchi rally. At a campaign rally in Yobe State on November 15, Atiku again promised to restore petrol and electricity subsidies, while pledging to address insecurity and create employment opportunities for young Nigerians. “Let me assure you that once I am elected president in 2027, I will bring back the fuel subsidy,” he said, adding that he would also restore electricity subsidy. He further promised that his administration would work to ensure peace returned to Yobe and other parts of the country, and that young Nigerians would have access to employment opportunities. In Kogi State on November 24 , Atiku campaigned on an “Affordable Life” message, promising to reduce fuel costs, support local production and improve Nigerians’ purchasing power. He said his proposals were aimed at easing the pressure on households, workers and small businesses. At the rally in Lokoja, he also pledged to revive and complete the Ajaokuta Steel Mill through foreign investment, without relying on government funding for the project. He promised to continue the Baro Port project by dredging the River Niger to enable the port to serve other states and create employment opportunities. “I want to promise you here today that I will revive and complete the Ajaokuta steel mill. item.title: Nothing wrong with ‘rig and die’, but innocent people must not be targeted — 2Baba
item.description: By Adegboyega Adeleye Singer-songwriter and record producer Innocent Idibia, popularly known as 2Baba, has said the “rig and die” slogan sounds correct as a response to election rigging, but warned that innocent people must not be caught up in the resulting violence. He spoke in an interview on Nigeria Info’s WhatsUpLagos show while responding to the slogan ahead of the 2027 elections. The ace singer said frustration over impunity had made calls for severe punishment understandable, while stressing that allegations of rigging must be proven. “You know when a situation gets to a certain point, like right now we’re like on a very mountainous keg of gunpowder right now. Desperate times make you make some kind of statements. This statement sounds correct. It should be like that, actually.” He said the slogan reflected a demand for stronger consequences for election rigging. “If you rig, the punishments should be very severe to deter people from rigging.” 2Baba added: “So the statement itself is rig or die. I don’t see anything that’s wrong with it. It’s like saying embezzle money and die. Na death penalty for China for embezzlement.” He said Nigeria needed serious deterrence for crimes, including kidnapping, and that people were frustrated by what he described as a lack of consequences. “We’re in a stage where we need, we need serious deterrence, anybody who kidnaps is supposed to face serious consequences. “Because it’s getting too much, and people are just getting away with everything. You understand what I’m saying? So for me, the statement itself, it shows the level of frustration. It shows the level of how things have gone by. So for me, I don’t see nothing wrong with that statement.” However, he warned against innocent people being harmed in the name of enforcing the slogan. “I just don’t want innocent people to get caught up in the process of this fight because some people might not rig, they might just be there. It could be jungle justice without proving that the person actually rigged.” He said the burden of proof should rest on the accusers, while reiterating his support for the statement. “So that’s where, that’s where it becomes dangerous. So the burden of proof should be on the accused person, but the statement in itself, I am in full support of it.” The post Nothing wrong with ‘rig and die’, but innocent people must not be targeted — 2Baba appeared first on Vanguard News .

item.title: Nvidia: Women Raise Concerns Over Jensen Huang’s Return
item.description: News of Jensen Huang’s shocking return to Nvidia had barely landed when President Donald Trump posted an AI-generated image of the Nvidia cofounder holding up a red bra, surrounded by security personnel whisking him offstage, blood streaked across his face. The image was based on a real photo taken in 2024 when Trump survived an assassination attempt during a campaign rally in Butler, Pennsylvania, and implied that Huang, too, had survived a bid to take him out. For many women, though, the image spoke insultingly to longstanding frustrations about sexism, double standards and a lack of accountability for men in power — across politics and business. Meanwhile, many “tech bros” rushed to Huang’s defense over the past couple of weeks. Billionaire Elon Musk was among many people who signed a petition calling for Huang’s reinstatement. Nvidia CEO Jensen Huang (R) speaks alongside US President Donald Trump about investing in America, at the White House in Washington, DC, on April 30, 2025. Photo by JIM WATSON / AFP Venture capitalist Jason Calacanis described Huang as a “hero” and downplayed the scandal that led to Huang’s resignation as less important than the United States winning the AI race against China. “They’re standing up for the idea that certain men can do whatever they want,” Cleo Capital Managing Director Sarah Kunst told AFP. Part of the problem might be “hero worship,” she said. It also reflects the tech industry’s mythology around “founder mode” — the belief that companies thrive when founders stay hands-on rather than cede control to executives. Huang resigned on November 12 from Nvidia, the company he cofounded and has led for more than three decades, amid allegations that he had multiple extramarital affairs, including one with a woman that US officials suspect was working for Chinese intelligence, triggering national security concerns. This screengrab from video footage by CTI obtained via AFPTV on November 9, 2026 shows Alice Huang (R), a Chinese executive linked to the data centre company called Megaspeed, attending a dinner hosted by Nvidia’s chief executive and co-founder Jensen Huang (L in black back facing camera) at a restaurant in Taipei on May 22, 2025, during Computex, the island’s top tech expo. Photo by – / VARIOUS SOURCES / AFP Another of Huanga’s alleged lovers was a subordinate at Nvidia. “This is a great example of why integrity matters,” Kunst said. “As soon as I heard about the honeypot element, it was clear to me that there were lapses in judgment that were really big.” On November 17, board Chairman Harvey Jones said the company “does not intend to reinstate Jensen as CEO.” Then President Donald Trump intervened. “I made the deal,” Trump told CNBC, referring to Huang’s reinstatement. Trump himself was found liable in 2023 for sexual assault and defamation and ordered to pay millions as punishment. item.title: I belong to APC but will protect all parties — Defence Minister
item.description: The Minister of Defence, Christopher Musa, has said his membership of the All Progressives Congress (APC) does not prevent him from carrying out his responsibility to provide security for all political parties ahead of the 2027 general elections. Musa, a retired general, said he was entitled to associate with the ruling party because he was no longer serving in the military. He made the remarks on Thursday during an interview on Arise Television, where he was asked to explain his participation in APC political activities and how he intended to separate his party affiliation from his official duties. “Well, I’m not a military man. I belong to APC, I’m allowed to do that,” he said. The former Chief of Defence Staff maintained that his appearances at political events were also an opportunity to assess security arrangements and ensure that security agencies were performing their duties. He stressed, however, that the responsibility applied to all political parties. “I always want to make sure that whatever is happening anywhere, I go there to ensure that the security forces are doing what they should, and we can do that for everybody. It’s not just for APC. “We are free-minded, we are fair-minded to everybody. We want Nigeria to be safe. We’ll never be a party to any violence,” he said. The minister said President Bola Tinubu had repeatedly cautioned members of his administration against electoral violence. “I know the President has told us on several occasions when we meet, ‘I do not want a violent election. It is not worth it,’” he added. Musa also pledged that the Ministry of Defence and the Armed Forces would collaborate with political parties and other stakeholders to ensure credible elections in 2027. “Nigerians must understand that we must make our elections free and fair and credible. So we, members of the Armed Forces and the Defence, will ensure that we work together with everyone to make the elections free. “We want every Nigerian to be free to come out and vote for whoever he wants,” he said. On complaints by opposition parties about political violence, Musa argued that disagreements within political parties could also trigger clashes. “Within all the parties, yes! We have found sometimes you see them because somebody feels somebody shouldn’t be there or his name was replaced for whatever reason, then he wants to sabotage from within. So the enemy is not only outside, it’s also within. “Whether the opposition or the party in government, violence is a no-no. And Defence is standing on its feet to ensure that the coming election is free and fair. Whatever it takes for us to do that, we will do that,” he said. The minister urged Nigerians to reject attempts by politicians to recruit them for violent activities, warning that those who lost their lives in political clashes could not be brought back. “We believe that if people are sensitised quite well and they see the folly of going into what they are doing, I mean, look at the few ones that h

item.title: Trump insists Nvidia CEO not a security threat
item.description: US President Donald Trump said Thursday that he had seen sufficient information that Nvidia’s Jensen Huang was not a security threat, while touting his administration’s intervention to save the scandal-plagued CEO’s job as “a great thing” for the world. “I think he’s absolutely fine,” Trump told reporters at his Mar-a-Lago estate. Asked by AFP how he could be sure when the Justice Department would not confirm it had conducted a thorough investigation into Huang, Trump said his belief was based on “information I have, which is a lot of information.” Huang, a key figure in the AI revolution, was forced to resign earlier this month after revelations that he had an affair with a business executive who reportedly has ties to Chinese intelligence and whose company may have helped China obtain advanced chips in violation of US export controls. His sudden resignation saw the stock price of Nvidia plummet, before a shock decision by the board to reinstate him saw a partial rebound. Trump revealed that he and other officials in his administration have worked behind the scenes to push for Huang to be reinstated, in a highly unusual intervention by the government into a top company’s decision making. “I just thought, I saw that what was happening with the company, what was happening with the stock, and I think it’s a great thing that he’s going back,” Trump said Thursday. “So I really… think I did a great thing for our country and even for the world,” Trump said of the effort to back Huang. Asked if he had spoken with Huang since his reinstatement was announced, Trump said no, but then later said: “When I did speak to him, he is so happy to be going back. He calls it his second term.” He also praised Huang’s wife as “phenomenal.” The post Trump insists Nvidia CEO not a security threat appeared first on Vanguard News .

item.title: 2027: 2Baba backs ‘rig and die’ slogan, demands severe penalties
item.description: Nigerian music star, Innocent Idibia, popularly known as 2Baba, has backed the controversial “rig and die” slogan associated with the Nigeria Democratic Congress (NDC), saying anyone caught manipulating election results in 2027 should face severe punishment. The singer, however, cautioned against innocent people being victimised in the process, insisting that elections should not be treated as warfare. He made the remarks on Thursday during an interview on Nigeria Info 99.3, where he described Nigeria’s political atmosphere as tense and said the slogan reflected growing public frustration over the country’s situation. “You know, when the situation gets to a certain point, like right now, we’re on a very mountainous keg of gunpowder right now. Desperate times make people make some kinds of statements. “The statement sounds correct, right? It sounds correct. It should be like that, actually. For the circumstances. Like, if you rig, the punishments will be very severe to deter people from rigging,” 2Baba said. The singer said he saw nothing wrong with the slogan, arguing that stringent penalties would discourage electoral malpractice. “The statement itself is ‘rig and die’. I don’t see anything that’s wrong with it. It’s like saying embezzlement and die. Now, there’s that penalty for embezzlement in China,” he said. 2Baba also called for severe consequences for kidnappers, particularly those targeting schools, arguing that the absence of adequate deterrence had allowed criminal activities to persist. “We’re in a state where we need serious deterrence for anybody who kidnaps in our schools to face serious consequences, so that others will not do it. Because it’s getting too much and people are just getting away with everything,” he said. The ‘African Queen’ crooner said the slogan reflected the level of frustration among Nigerians but warned against punishing people without evidence of wrongdoing. “For me, the statement itself shows the level of frustration. It shows the level of how things have gone bad. So, for me, I don’t see anything wrong with that statement. “I just don’t want innocent people to get caught up in the process of this,” he added. During the interview, the presenter recalled 2Baba’s longstanding advocacy for peaceful electoral participation, including his message urging Nigerians to vote rather than fight during elections. Asked about Nigerians who might sell their votes because of economic hardship, the singer described the situation as unfortunate, noting that people facing difficult conditions could easily become vulnerable to manipulation. He also called for proper reorientation, urging Nigerians to address internal challenges rather than allow external interests to influence the country. The “rig and die” slogan has featured prominently in political discussions ahead of the 2027 general elections, particularly among supporters of the NDC and its presidential candidate, Peter Obi. item.title: CeBIH, NIMC to explore digital identity for financial inclusion, growth
item.description: By Babajide Komolafe The Committee of e-Business Industry Heads (CeBIH) and the National Identity Management Commission (NIMC) are set to explore how digital identity can drive financial inclusion, trust and economic growth at the 2026 CeBIH Annual Conference scheduled for December 1 and 2 in Lagos. The conference, themed “Digital Identity: A Catalyst for Financial Inclusion, Trust and Growth,” will bring together policymakers, regulators, financial services leaders and technology innovators to examine the role of identity infrastructure in Nigeria’s digital financial ecosystem. Speaking at a press conference on the theme of the conference, Chairman of CeBIH, Mrs. Abidemi Asunmo, said the future of financial services and the broader digital economy depended significantly on reliable, secure and accessible digital identity infrastructure. “A trusted digital identity ecosystem has implications far beyond registration and identification. It can help address some of the structural barriers to financial inclusion.’’ Gbolahan Oluwatobiloba, Lagos State Coordinator, NIMC, said identity was the foundation of economic development, security and trust. “Identity is the foundation of everything, not just the financial sector, the security sector or the identity ecosystem. When you remove identity, your security will be affected, because how do you secure people you don’t know?” he said. Vice Chairman of CeBIH and Chairman of the Conference Planning Committee, Abednigo Ugwueke, said participants would examine how trusted digital identity could improve customer onboarding, strengthen Know Your Customer processes, enhance identity verification, reduce fraud and expand access to financial services. The conference is expected to feature key government and industry personalities, including NIMC Director-General, Engr. Abisoye Coker-Odusote; Executive Chairman of the Nigeria Revenue Service, Dr. Zach Adedeji; National Commissioner and Chief Executive Officer of the Nigeria Data Protection Commission, Dr. Vincent Olatunji; and Comptroller-General of the Nigeria Immigration Service, Kemi Nanna Nandap. Kayode Olubiyi, Head of Digital Payments, UBA, representing the CeBIH Advisory Council, said customers increasingly prioritised security and trust in banking. The post CeBIH, NIMC to explore digital identity for financial inclusion, growth appeared first on Vanguard News .

item.title: UNICEF, NGE, Lagos govt to tackle child survival, education challenges
item.description: By Ch ioma Obinna & Juliet Umeh Stakeholders, yesterday, called for stronger collaboration among government, the media, private sector and communities to address challenges threatening child survival, education and development in Nigeria. The stakeholders include the United Nations Children’s Fund, UNICEF, Nigerian Guild of Editors, NGE, Lagos State Government and Airtel Nigeria made the call at the 2026 World Children’s Day High-Level Media Symposium themed: ‘Every Child Alive, Thriving and Learning: A Shared Responsibility’ in Lagos. Speaking at the event organised by UNICEF Nigeria in partnership with the NGE and Diamond Awards for Media Excellence, DAME, President of the NGE, Mr. Eze Anaba, said the responsibility of ensuring that Nigerian children survived, received quality education and realised their potential rested on all stakeholders, not government alone. Anaba cited a UNICEF report indicating that 18.3 million Nigerian children were out of school, describing the figure as alarming and calling for urgent collective action. “In a country of over 200 million people, 18 million-plus of that population is on the streets, not going to school. It’s not only alarming; it’s a collective responsibility,” he said. He challenged media organisations, private sector players, community leaders and parents to examine their contributions towards addressing the problem. “Have we reminded the government? Community leaders, have they done their part? Has the media done enough? The private sector, has it done enough?” he asked. Anaba urged stakeholders to develop an action plan with specific commitments, stressing that annual commemorations must translate into measurable improvements in children’s lives. Earlier, UNICEF Chief of Communication, Advocacy and Partnership, Ms. Lone Hvass, said: “Survival, education and learning are deeply interconnected. A child who is out of school is denied much more than education. He or she is denied opportunities for protection, participation and the possibility of realising their full potential. “The media does much more than report on children’s issues. Media helps determine which issues receive public attention, which voices are heard, which assumptions are challenged, and which movements are followed through,” Hvass said. She urged journalists to move beyond episodic coverage and headlines to sustained reporting that connects individual experiences with systemic challenges, provides evidence and exposes gaps in policy implementation. Sanwo-Olu Also speaking, Lagos State First Lady, Dr. Claudiana Sanwo-Olu, said children were not merely beneficiaries of government policies but individuals with rights, aspirations, talents and opinions whose voices deserved to be heard in decisions affecting them. item.title: CBN appoints Murtala Mohammed acting MD of Keystone Bank
item.description: By Emma Ujah, Abuja Bureau Chief The Central Bank of Nigeria (CBN) has appointed Mr. Murtala Mohammed as Acting Managing Director/Chief Executive Officer of Keystone Bank Limited. The appointment, announced on Thursday night, took effect on November 26, 2026, with Mohammed succeeding Mr. Hassan Imam. In a statement, the CBN Director of Corporate Communications and Investor Relations, Mr. Michael Akuka, said the appointment was made in exercise of the powers conferred on the apex bank by the Banks and Other Financial Institutions Act, 2020. He said the appointment was consistent with the CBN’s mandate to promote a safe, sound and stable financial system. “The appointment is consistent with the CBN’s mandate to promote a safe, sound and stable financial system,” Akuka said. The CBN reassured depositors, customers and other stakeholders that Keystone Bank remained fully operational, with banking services continuing as normal and depositors’ funds secure. “The CBN wishes to reassure depositors, customers and other stakeholders that Keystone Bank Limited remains fully operational, with banking services continuing as normal and depositors’ funds remaining secure. “The CBN remains committed to safeguarding depositors’ interests and ensuring the continued soundness and stability of Nigeria’s banking sector,” the statement said.
